raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## What

`tokenize_formatted_sft_sample` (the unpacked SFT path, the default when sequence packing is off) shifts `labels` to next-token targets (`labels[i] = input_ids[i+1]`), but leaves `loss_mask` on **input** positions. The SFT loss is `CE(logits[i], labels[i]) * loss_mask[i]`, so the mask is off by one:

- the **first response token is never a target**;
- the **token after the response is**. With no EOS appended, that token is the pad id.

For tokenizers without a pad token, pad falls back to EOS, which hides the bug (Mistral, SmolLM3). Models with a **dedicated pad token** are trained to emit it after every answer: phi-4 (`<|dummy_85|>`) and granite-4.1 (`<|pad|>`).

This PR shifts the mask to label positions (`loss_mask[i] = supervised[i+1]`, last position 0) in both branches of the function. The packed path (`packing.py`) already does this, and so does Megatron-Bridge (`loss_mask = item["loss_mask"][1:]`).

## How it was found

We ran a convergence check that fine-tunes from the released checkpoint on alpaca-cleaned (Alpaca formatter, packing off, seq 1024, global batch 16). It compares the iteration-1 loss with the mean loss of the same model in `transformers` on the same alpaca prompts, scoring only the response tokens.

| Model | Pad token | Iteration-1 / reference |
|---|---|---|
| Mistral-7B-v0.3 | none (falls back to EOS) | 0.94–1.03 |
| SmolLM3-3B-Base | none (falls back to EOS) | 1.05–1.14 |
| phi-4 | `<|dummy_85|>` | 1.18–1.28 |
| granite-4.1-3b | `<|pad|>` | 1.23–1.28 |

The ranges cover runs at 1, 2, 4 and 8 GPUs. The loss curves themselves fall normally, so nothing else looked wrong.

## Tests

`test_tokenize_formatted_sft_sample_targets_exactly_the_response_tokens`, for both `bridge_compat_inline_bos` settings, with a tokenizer whose pad id differs from EOS:

- the scored targets (`labels[loss_mask == 1]`) are exactly the response tokens, in order, plus the appended EOS on the Bridge-compatible path;
- the pad id is never a target;
- the last position is masked.

Before the fix the test reads `[response[1:]..., pad]`; after it, `[response...]`.

`pytest tests/unit_tests/backends/megatron/test_sft_abstractions.py tests/unit_tests/backends/megatron/test_sft_dataset_offline.py tests/unit_tests/backends/megatron/test_messages_format.py`: 17 passed (CPU).

## Stop token

The default unpacked path now appends a supervised EOS after a supervised response, as the `bridge_compat_inline_bos` path already does, so every tokenizer learns to stop. Before, only tokenizers whose pad resolved to EOS trained a stop token, and only by accident of the misaligned mask. The packed default path (`packing._tokenize_no_pad`) still appends no EOS. That predates this PR and is left for a follow-up.

## Follow-up

We will re-run the phi-4 and granite fine-tuning checks with this change and post the iteration-1 ratios here.

Re-ran the fine-tuning check (from the released checkpoint, alpaca-cleaned, 2000 iterations, 8 GPUs, same data, seed and global batch) with this change applied:

| Model | Iteration-1 / reference, before | after |
|---|---|---|
| granite-4.1-3b | 1.28 | 1.05 |
| phi-4 | 1.25 | 1.09 |

The rest of the curve is unchanged (late/early about 0.96 for granite and 0.98 for phi-4, as before). Runs at 1, 2 and 4 GPUs are in progress; I'll add them here.

Full results with this change, fine-tuning from the released checkpoint on alpaca-cleaned (2000 iterations, same data, seed and global batch at every GPU count). Iteration-1 loss over a `transformers` reference on the same samples:

| Model | GPUs | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| granite-4.1-3b | 1 | 1.19 | 0.99 |
| granite-4.1-3b | 2 | 1.24 | 1.05 |
| granite-4.1-3b | 4 | 1.23 | 1.01 |
| granite-4.1-3b | 8 | 1.28 | 1.05 |
| phi-4 | 1 | 1.18 | 1.02 |
| phi-4 | 2 | 1.28 | 1.14 |
| phi-4 | 4 | 1.21 | 1.05 |
| phi-4 | 8 | 1.25 | 1.09 |

The first step is deterministic for a given GPU count (a repeat of phi-4 at 2 GPUs gave 1.1385 both times); the spread across GPU counts comes from how the samples are split across data-parallel ranks. Models without a dedicated pad token (Mistral-7B-v0.3, SmolLM3-3B-Base) were at 0.94-1.14 before and are unaffected by the change.

Thanks for the reviews. Addressed in cec8e6cd:

1. **Stop token for pad==EOS tokenizers (PR Pundit #1).** Agreed. The old off-by-one only trained a stop token by accident. The default unpacked path now appends a supervised EOS after a supervised response, as the `bridge_compat_inline_bos` path already does, and then truncates. This is a behaviour change: every tokenizer now learns to stop, not only those whose pad happened to be EOS. The packed default path (`packing._tokenize_no_pad`) also appends no EOS. That predates this PR, so I've left it for a follow-up.
2. **Tests (PR Pundit #2, Copilot).** The special ids now sit outside `MockTokenizer`'s hashed 0–9999 range, so the test no longer depends on the salted hash. I checked it with several `PYTHONHASHSEED` values. The targets are checked for a dedicated-pad tokenizer and for a pad==EOS one, on both paths, plus a sample that exactly fills `max_seq_length` and a response truncated by it. I removed the `loss_mask[-1] == 0` assertion, which could not fail. Two of the new tests fail on the previous code.
3. **Docstring (PR Pundit #3).** It now states that `loss_mask` is in label space, with the last position always 0, so callers must not shift it again.
4. **Comment (PR Pundit #4).** Trimmed to the alignment rule and the cross-reference to `packing.py` and Bridge.

The SFT unit tests pass on CPU (`test_sft_abstractions.py`, `test_sft_dataset_offline.py`, `test_messages_format.py`: 19 passed).

### 🟡 Changes recommended The test can fail under Python’s randomized hash seed because special-token IDs overlap with ordinary token IDs; both special IDs need to be reserved outside the mock tokenizer’s 0–9999 range.
1 open issue - [Reserve special-token IDs outside the mock tokenizer range](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1351#discussion_r4425411481) · New
What changed in this PR This PR fixes an off-by-one loss mask in unpacked Megatron SFT preprocessing, aligning supervision with next-token labels. **Changes:** - Shift the loss mask to score response targets correctly and keep the final position masked. - Add regression coverage for both `bridge_compat_inline_bos` settings using distinct pad and EOS IDs. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `tests/​unit_tests/​backends/​megatron/​test_sft_abstractions.py` | Adds assertions for exact supervised targets, pad exclusion, and final-position masking. | | `primus/​backends/​megatron/​sft/​preprocessing.py` | Shifts the supervision mask to match labels and documents the alignment. |
Review effort: Balanced

The inherited `MockTokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids()` returns `hash(token) % 10000`, so these special-token IDs overlap with ordinary token IDs. If a response token hashes to `9999`, `assert tok.pad not in targets` fails even with the correct mask, making the test dependent on Python's randomized hash seed. Reserve both special-token IDs outside the mock tokenizer's 0–9999 range.

### PR Pundit review
4 findings, 1 as comments on the diff below.

| # | | Finding | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 🟠 | Unpacked SFT with pad==EOS tokenizers no longer trains the stop token: this PR shifted the mask | `primus/backends/megatron/sft/preprocessing.py:234` ↓ |
| 2 | 🔵 | Truncation, exact-fit, pad==EOS and packed-parity regressions pass: this PR's test covers one padded case | `tests/unit_tests/backends/megatron/test_sft_abstractions.py:101` |
| 3 | 🔵 | Callers of the re-exported helper could double-shift the mask: this PR left the docstring stale | `primus/backends/megatron/sft/preprocessing.py:149` |
| 4 | 🔵 | Alignment comment embeds bug history and phi-4/granite benchmark numbers that will go stale | `primus/backends/megatron/sft/preprocessing.py:224` |

<details><summary>Nits and less certain findings (3)</summary>

**2. Truncation, exact-fit, pad==EOS and packed-parity regressions pass: this PR's test covers one padded case** (`tests/unit_tests/backends/megatron/test_sft_abstractions.py:101`)

The new test checks one short sample padded to `max_seq_length=64` with a BOS-less `MockTokenizer`. Its `loss_mask[-1] == 0` assertion cannot fail: the new code builds `loss_mask_tensor` with `zeros_like` and fills only `[:-1]`, so the last position is 0 by construction. Also not covered: truncation inside the response, a sample that fills `max_seq_length` exactly, and parity of (`labels`, `loss_mask`) with `packing.py`, which the comment says this mirrors. Not covered either: a BOS-per-segment tokenizer on the `bridge_compat_inline_bos` path, and a tokenizer whose pad id equals EOS. In that last case the shift no longer scores the trailing pad/EOS as a target on the non-inline path, so the model is no longer trained to stop; a test would pin that behaviour change.

**Who is affected:** Maintainers relying on the unit tests to guard the unpacked SFT loss-mask contract (mainly pad==eos tokenizers and truncated samples).

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**3. Callers of the re-exported helper could double-shift the mask: this PR left the docstring stale** (`primus/backends/megatron/sft/preprocessing.py:149`)

The `tokenize_formatted_sft_sample` docstring does not say that the returned `loss_mask` is now in label space (`loss_mask[i] = supervised[i+1]`, scoring `labels[i] = input_ids[i+1]`) or that the last position is always 0. That contract is explained only in an inline comment. No in-tree caller shifts the mask itself, so nothing double-shifts today. Stating the contract in the docstring would protect future external users of the re-exported helper.

**Origin:** latent

**Who is affected:** Only a future or external caller of the re-exported helper that assumes the mask is in input space; no current Primus code path.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**4. Alignment comment embeds bug history and phi-4/granite benchmark numbers that will go stale** (`primus/backends/megatron/sft/preprocessing.py:224`)

The new 11-line comment narrates the old bug and cites the phi-4/granite '18-28% above a transformers reference' measurement. That history will go stale and belongs in the commit message or PR body. Keep only the alignment rule (`labels[i] = input_ids[i+1]`, `loss_mask[i] = supervised[i+1]`) and the cross-reference to `packing.py`/Bridge.

_An independent check of the code found this probably does not apply: The parallel comment in head/primus/backends/megatron/sft/packing.py (around lines 340-346) also records the failure mode and a measured loss gap ('~13.6 instead of ~4.3 for Llama-2 on SQuAD'), so the finding's premise that packing.py has the rationale without history is false. The new comment matches that existing convention and states the alignment rule correctly, so the request is a style preference that runs against the project's practice._

</details>

**1. 🟠 Should fix: Unpacked SFT with pad==EOS tokenizers no longer trains the stop token: this PR shifted the mask**

After this PR the default unpacked path (`bridge_compat_inline_bos=False`) supervises no stop token. Before, for tokenizers without a dedicated pad (`_resolve_pad_token_id` falls back to `eod`/`eos_token_id`), the off-by-one mask made the first pad, which equals EOS, a target; that was an accident of the misalignment this PR fixes. The missing EOS itself predates the PR: the default path never appends one, and the packed default path (`packing._tokenize_no_pad`) already trains without EOS. Consider appending a supervised EOS on the default path, as the inline-BOS path does, so unpacked pad==EOS runs keep stop-token supervision.

**Who is affected:** Unpacked Megatron SFT runs with the default `sft_bridge_compat_inline_bos: false` and a tokenizer that has no dedicated pad token (pad resolves to eod/eos, e.g. Llama-2 / GPT-2 style), for samples shorter than `max_seq_length`.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

### 🟡 Changes recommended Active issues leave assistant stop tokens unsupervised in chatml and openai/messages samples and cause unnecessary repeated tokenization of long conversation prefixes beyond the sequence limit.
2 open issues - [Deferred truncation makes long-sample tokenization unnecessarily expensive](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1351#discussion_r4429579369) · New - [ChatML and OpenAI formats lose assistant stop-token supervision](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1351#discussion_r4429579386) · New
1 resolved since last review - [Reserve special-token IDs outside the mock tokenizer range](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1351#discussion_r4425411481)
Review effort: Balanced

Deferring truncation until after mask construction prevents the prefix-tokenization loop from stopping once it passes `max_seq_length`. Long multi-turn samples now re-tokenize every growing conversation prefix, even though the excess tokens are discarded, and `SFTDataset.__getitem__` repeats this work on each access. Restore truncation before constructing the mask, while retaining the later truncation to discard an appended EOS when the sequence is already full.

+        normalize_sft_sample({"instruction": "What is SFT?", "response": response})
+    )
+
+
+def _targets(formatted, tok, max_seq_length, inline_bos=False):
+    """The scored targets: ``labels`` where ``loss_mask`` is 1."""
+    input_ids, labels, loss_mask = tokenize_formatted_sft_sample(
+        formatted_sample=formatted,
+        tokenizer=tok,
+        max_seq_length=max_seq_length,
+        bridge_compat_inline_bos=inline_bos,
+    )
+    assert input_ids.shape == labels.shape == loss_mask.shape == (max_seq_length,)
+    return labels[loss_mask.bool()].tolist(), input_ids
+
+
+def test_tokenize_formatted_sft_sample_targets_exactly_the_response_then_eos():
+    """The scored targets are the response tokens in order (the first one included), then one EOS, on both
+    paths; never the pad token after the response."""
+    formatted = _sft_sample()
+    for tok in (PaddedTokenizer(), PadIsEosTokenizer()):
+        response = tok.convert_tokens_to_ids(tok.tokenize("SFT is supervised fine-tuning."))
+        for inline_bos in (False, True):
+            targets, _ = _targets(formatted, tok, 64, inline_bos)
+            assert targets == response + [tok.eos]
+            if getattr(tok, "pad", None) is not None:
+                assert tok.pad not in targets
+
+
+def test_a_sample_that_fills_max_seq_length_keeps_every_target():
+    """Exact fit: the last position has no target, so the EOS is the last scored target."""
+    tok = PaddedTokenizer()
+    formatted = _sft_sample()
+    full = len(tok.tokenize(formatted.text)) + 1  # + the appended EOS
+    targets, input_ids = _targets(formatted, tok, full)
+    assert targets == tok.convert_tokens_to_ids(tok.tokenize("SFT is supervised fine-tuning.")) + [tok.eos]
+    assert tok.pad not in input_ids.tolist()
+
+
+def test_a_response_cut_by_max_seq_length_scores_only_the_tokens_that_fit():
+    """Truncation inside the response: every response token that fits is a target (predicted from the position
+    before it), and no EOS (it was cut off)."""
+    tok = PaddedTokenizer()
+    formatted = _sft_sample("one two three four five six seven eight")
+    prompt_len = len(tok.tokenize(formatted.text)) - 8
+    limit = prompt_len + 3  # the prompt and the first three response tokens
+    targets, input_ids = _targets(formatted, tok, limit)
+    assert targets == tok.convert_tokens_to_ids("one two three".split())
+    assert input_ids.tolist()[-1] == tok.convert_tokens_to_ids(["three"])[0]
+
+

Re-ran the fine-tuning check (from the released checkpoint, alpaca-cleaned, 2000 iterations, 8 GPUs, same data, seed and global batch) with this change applied:

| Model | Iteration-1 / reference, before | after |
|---|---|---|
| granite-4.1-3b | 1.28 | 1.05 |
| phi-4 | 1.25 | 1.09 |

The rest of the curve is unchanged (late/early about 0.96 for granite and 0.98 for phi-4, as before). Runs at 1, 2 and 4 GPUs are in progress; I'll add them here.

Full results with this change, fine-tuning from the released checkpoint on alpaca-cleaned (2000 iterations, same data, seed and global batch at every GPU count). Iteration-1 loss over a `transformers` reference on the same samples:

| Model | GPUs | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| granite-4.1-3b | 1 | 1.19 | 0.99 |
| granite-4.1-3b | 2 | 1.24 | 1.05 |
| granite-4.1-3b | 4 | 1.23 | 1.01 |
| granite-4.1-3b | 8 | 1.28 | 1.05 |
| phi-4 | 1 | 1.18 | 1.02 |
| phi-4 | 2 | 1.28 | 1.14 |
| phi-4 | 4 | 1.21 | 1.05 |
| phi-4 | 8 | 1.25 | 1.09 |

The first step is deterministic for a given GPU count (a repeat of phi-4 at 2 GPUs gave 1.1385 both times); the spread across GPU counts comes from how the samples are split across data-parallel ranks. Models without a dedicated pad token (Mistral-7B-v0.3, SmolLM3-3B-Base) were at 0.94-1.14 before and are unaffected by the change.

Thanks for the reviews. Addressed in cec8e6cd:

1. **Stop token for pad==EOS tokenizers (PR Pundit #1).** Agreed. The old off-by-one only trained a stop token by accident. The default unpacked path now appends a supervised EOS after a supervised response, as the `bridge_compat_inline_bos` path already does, and then truncates. This is a behaviour change: every tokenizer now learns to stop, not only those whose pad happened to be EOS. The packed default path (`packing._tokenize_no_pad`) also appends no EOS. That predates this PR, so I've left it for a follow-up.
2. **Tests (PR Pundit #2, Copilot).** The special ids now sit outside `MockTokenizer`'s hashed 0–9999 range, so the test no longer depends on the salted hash. I checked it with several `PYTHONHASHSEED` values. The targets are checked for a dedicated-pad tokenizer and for a pad==EOS one, on both paths, plus a sample that exactly fills `max_seq_length` and a response truncated by it. I removed the `loss_mask[-1] == 0` assertion, which could not fail. Two of the new tests fail on the previous code.
3. **Docstring (PR Pundit #3).** It now states that `loss_mask` is in label space, with the last position always 0, so callers must not shift it again.
4. **Comment (PR Pundit #4).** Trimmed to the alignment rule and the cross-reference to `packing.py` and Bridge.

The SFT unit tests pass on CPU (`test_sft_abstractions.py`, `test_sft_dataset_offline.py`, `test_messages_format.py`: 19 passed).

<details><summary>Nits and less certain findings (3)</summary>

**2. Truncation, exact-fit, pad==EOS and packed-parity regressions pass: this PR's test covers one padded case** (`tests/unit_tests/backends/megatron/test_sft_abstractions.py:101`)

The new test checks one short sample padded to `max_seq_length=64` with a BOS-less `MockTokenizer`. Its `loss_mask[-1] == 0` assertion cannot fail: the new code builds `loss_mask_tensor` with `zeros_like` and fills only `[:-1]`, so the last position is 0 by construction. Also not covered: truncation inside the response, a sample that fills `max_seq_length` exactly, and parity of (`labels`, `loss_mask`) with `packing.py`, which the comment says this mirrors. Not covered either: a BOS-per-segment tokenizer on the `bridge_compat_inline_bos` path, and a tokenizer whose pad id equals EOS. In that last case the shift no longer scores the trailing pad/EOS as a target on the non-inline path, so the model is no longer trained to stop; a test would pin that behaviour change.

**Who is affected:** Maintainers relying on the unit tests to guard the unpacked SFT loss-mask contract (mainly pad==eos tokenizers and truncated samples).

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**3. Callers of the re-exported helper could double-shift the mask: this PR left the docstring stale** (`primus/backends/megatron/sft/preprocessing.py:149`)

The `tokenize_formatted_sft_sample` docstring does not say that the returned `loss_mask` is now in label space (`loss_mask[i] = supervised[i+1]`, scoring `labels[i] = input_ids[i+1]`) or that the last position is always 0. That contract is explained only in an inline comment. No in-tree caller shifts the mask itself, so nothing double-shifts today. Stating the contract in the docstring would protect future external users of the re-exported helper.

**Origin:** latent

**Who is affected:** Only a future or external caller of the re-exported helper that assumes the mask is in input space; no current Primus code path.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**4. Alignment comment embeds bug history and phi-4/granite benchmark numbers that will go stale** (`primus/backends/megatron/sft/preprocessing.py:224`)

The new 11-line comment narrates the old bug and cites the phi-4/granite '18-28% above a transformers reference' measurement. That history will go stale and belongs in the commit message or PR body. Keep only the alignment rule (`labels[i] = input_ids[i+1]`, `loss_mask[i] = supervised[i+1]`) and the cross-reference to `packing.py`/Bridge.

_An independent check of the code found this probably does not apply: The parallel comment in head/primus/backends/megatron/sft/packing.py (around lines 340-346) also records the failure mode and a measured loss gap ('~13.6 instead of ~4.3 for Llama-2 on SQuAD'), so the finding's premise that packing.py has the rationale without history is false. The new comment matches that existing convention and states the alignment rule correctly, so the request is a style preference that runs against the project's practice._

</details>
